title: Johnson the clarinetist and the Mexico trip
summary: A clarinetist named Johnson went to Mexico with them; the band was short on good men and lost Walter Brundy.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Does he know a fella named Johnson played clarinet?
Do you know a fella by the name of Johnson played clarinet? Johnson? Yeah, this black fella. Yeah, he wasn't much, but he was well known around there. He the one who went to Mexico with us.

What is his real name? Full name? I know Johnson. He's wife. We had a wife. He looked like a white guy. Yeah, he wasn't much on the kind of... We didn't have but four good men when we went to Mexico. But you see, he did his picture itself. After that, he backed out. He said they were scared to go to Mexico because they had so much revolution. So I know some Mexican here at the corner from my house. I went and asked them to ask me what part. I told them, you can change. Oh, they say it's fine. Just like here. That's where I went with him, you know what I mean? I'll tell you, you know. They said, pick up Johnson. I sent for Walter Brundy. Walter Brundy got back there in time, but he didn't know where to meet us at. And we didn't meet where they told us we were going to meet. When we went out to one doc, they met another one. That's where Walter Brundy missed it, you see. If Walter had recorded, we'd have a good band, you see. Now most of all them good bands in Mexico, them part of the Reed. Every time he turned around, they got a conservatory over there, you know. And he didn't go down and get a free lesson. Who wants to get them? I'm not too long, you know. Oh, yeah. I cut the code easy.
